suggestions.title: The Empire Strikes Back
suggestions.description: The sequel that turned a space adventure into a myth. Luke Skywalker trains with Yoda in the swamps of Dagobah while Han Solo and Princess Leia flee the Empire across the galaxy — and Darth Vader waits on Cloud City with a revelation that detonated cinema history. Irvin Kershner deepened every character, staged the breathtaking Hoth battle, and landed the most quoted plot twist ever filmed. 8.7 on IMDb, and still the high-water mark of the Star Wars saga — widely called the greatest sequel ever made.

suggestions.title: The Usual Suspects
suggestions.description: Five career criminals are hauled into a New York lineup and walk out as a crew, pulling a job that ends in a burning boat and twenty-seven dead bodies. The lone survivor, the limping Verbal Kint, spins the story for a federal agent — and Kevin Spacey's Oscar-winning turn is the calm at the centre of the best con in 1990s cinema. Roger Ebert called the ending a magic trick, and it still holds up: a labyrinth of a screenplay by Christopher McQuarrie that rewards a second viewing. 8.5 on IMDb.

suggestions.title: The Pianist
suggestions.description: Wladyslaw Szpilman was playing Chopin live on Warsaw radio when the first shells hit. Based on his memoir, Roman Polanski's film follows the pianist through the ghetto, the transports and the ruins of a flattened city — surviving on luck, silence and a German officer's mercy. Adrien Brody won a Best Actor Oscar for a performance of almost unbearable restraint, and Polanski took Best Director and the Palme d'Or. A quiet, devastating counterpart to Schindler's List. 8.5 on IMDb.
